question: A tool named analyze_content was originally built to summarize any pasted content, including emails and internal notes, but its description was never updated after a web-specific successor tool was introduced. The model now sometimes calls the general tool for web-only tasks. What is the recommended remediation?
options: A) Rename the general tool to reflect its remaining scope, and update its description to exclude the case the newer tool now handles.
B) Increase the priority weight of the newer tool in the backend routing configuration without touching either tool's description.
C) Leave both tools with their original names, but ask users to specify which tool they want by internal ID every time.
D) Delete the description text from both tools so the model relies entirely on tool names for disambiguation.
correct_answers: A) Rename the general tool to reflect its remaining scope, and update its description to exclude the case the newer tool now handles.
explanations: Correct. Updating the general tool's name and description to reflect its narrower remaining scope removes the overlap with the newer, web-specific tool.
Incorrect. A backend priority weight influences routing outside of the model's own reasoning and does not resolve the description staleness that caused the confusion.
Incorrect. Requiring users to reference internal tool IDs defeats the purpose of natural-language tool selection and does not address the stale description.
Incorrect. Removing description text eliminates useful information entirely rather than correcting the specific stale claim about scope.
